articles.title: Gerard Moreno ingresa en el “club de los cinco” del Villarreal
articles.standfirst: El delantero alcanza los 330 partidos oficiales e iguala a Santi Cazorla en la quinta plaza histórica del Submarino.
articles.summary: El delantero alcanza los 330 partidos oficiales e iguala a Santi Cazorla en la quinta plaza histórica del Submarino.
articles.body: Gerard Moreno sigue haciendo historia en amarillo. El delantero del Villarreal ya comparte con un mito como Santi Cazorla la quinta posición en el ranking de futbolistas con más partidos oficiales en la historia del club. Los 330 encuentros que ha alcanzado tras medirse al Nápoles le sitúan en un grupo reservado a los nombres propios de la entidad. Un reconocimiento más para un futbolista que lleva años marcando una época en La Cerámica. Ante el Nápoles el catalán partió de inicio para sumar un partido más en su trayectoria en el club castellonense. El undécimo que disputa en Liga de Campeones y que se une a los 257 que ha jugado en La Liga (tanto en Primera como de Segunda), 20 en Copa, 36 en Europa League, 5 en Conference y una final de Supercopa de Europa.Y lo pudo celebrar con una importantísima victoria. Desde su regreso en 2018, procedente del Espanyol, Gerard se ha convertido en mucho más que un goleador. Ante el Nápoles alcanzó los 330 partidos oficiales, una cifra que sería mucho más alta de no ser por las lesiones que le han perseguido durante las últimas temporadas La clasificación histórica tiene a Manu Trigueros en lo más alto, con 483 partidos oficiales. Le siguen Bruno Soriano, con 425; Mario Gaspar, con 423; y Marcos Senna, con 361. Gerard y Cazorla comparten la quinta plaza con 330 encuentros, El siguiente objetivo está marcado: acercarse a los registros de Senna y continuar escalando posiciones. Por delante tiene todavía 31 partidos para alcanzar al brasileño, una referencia de la historia amarilla. Gerard ya ha dejado su nombre grabado en los capítulos más importantes del Villarreal. Fue protagonista en la conquista de la Europa League de 2021 y se ha convertido en el máximo goleador de la entidad. Ahora, con 330 partidos, añade otra cifra de peso a un currículum que sigue creciendo.

articles.title: Barrios, sobre su dedicatoria a Koke: "He dicho que si marcaba, hacía eso y me ha salido solo"
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista atendió a los medios a la conclusión del choque
articles.summary: El centrocampista atendió a los medios a la conclusión del choque
articles.body: Pablo Barrios fue uno de los grandes protagonistas del partido del Atlético ante el Manchester United. Anotó el primer gol y brilló en el centro del campo. El mediocampista atendió a los medios de comunicación a la conclusión del duelo. La victoria: "Lo primero, además de por el equipo, era muy importante por Koke y por toda su familia, es un día muy duro para ellos. Esta victoria va para ellos". Dedicatoria del gol a Koke: "Ha sido una noticia muy dura para todos y he dicho que si marcaba, hacía eso y me ha salido solo". Gol: "El gol tan pronto nos ha ayudado a manejar luego el partido. Muy contentos por la victoria". Gran momento: "Ha sido un partido bueno del equipo, aunque ellos también nos han generado ocasiones. Hemos hecho un partido muy serio y hemos conseguido la primera victoria". Gol anulado por mano de Llorente: "No la he visto repetida, Marcos decía que no lo tenía claro. Yo no la he visto".

articles.title: Atletico Madrid beat Manchester United 2-0 as winless run continues
articles.summary: Michael Carrick’s Man Utd continue to search for a win as Atletico win 2-0 in UEFA Champions League.
articles.body:
Atletico Madrid eased to a 2-0 win over Manchester United in the Champions League on Tuesday to pile pressure on Red Devils coach Michael Carrick.

Pablo Barrios pounced inside the first minute for Diego Simeone’s side and after Leny Yoro’s 74th minute red card set United back further, Ademola Lookman added another for the hosts in Madrid.

Man United have made their worst domestic start in 40 years and this league phase defeat in the Spanish capital was another blow, with the team now winless in five games across all competitions.

Carrick handed Carlos Baleba his first start for the club since arriving from Brighton this summer, as well as pushing captain Bruno Fernandes out to the right side.

Atletico were without their skipper Koke, after the death of his mother, while coach Simeone selected Julian Alvarez from the off for the first time this season at the Metropolitano stadium, after he tried to force a departure this summer.

“Defend what we love,” Atletico fans ordered their supporters with a banner display before kick-off. The Rojiblancos were ahead after just 50 seconds.

Alex Baena found a way in behind United’s defence and cut the ball across for Barrios, with Ayden Heaven unable to keep the midfielder’s shot from crossing the line.

Bryan Mbuemo might have equalised for the visitors, nudging the ball through Cristian Romero’s legs but firing just wide.

Alejandro Grimaldo came inches away from extending Atletico’s lead with a free-kick which hit the angle between post and crossbar.

The hosts thought they had a second when Johnny Cardoso finished neatly from the edge of the box before half-time but the goal was disallowed after a VAR review showed the ball had struck Marcos Llorente’s hand during the build-up.

Alvarez, yet to score this season for Atletico, hit the post early in the second half.

United rallied and Fernandes’s lob drifted narrowly wide before the Portuguese playmaker hit the crossbar from the left of the box after a corner routine.

However, the three-time European champions suffered a setback when defender Yoro was harshly dismissed after a VAR review for bringing down Canada striker Jonathan David as the last man.

It opened the door for Atletico to grab their second, with David foiled by goalkeeper Senne Lammens but London-born Nigeria international Lookman on hand to tuck home the rebound after 79 minutes.

Carrick withdrew playmaker Fernandes, looking ahead to the weekend visit to face rivals Leeds in the English top flight, where improvement is badly needed.

Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved from United substitute Matheus Cunha in the final stages but there was no way back for United.

Simeone’s side were able to claim their first points after an opening defeat at Liverpool.

articles.title: Cardiff City 5-1 Watford: Pressure on Hornets boss Alessio Dionisi increases as Jack Moylan scores twice in hammering
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Cardiff and Watford at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday; Jack Moylan scores twice as the Bluebirds inflict a fourth straight defeat on Alession Dionisi's Hornets
articles.body:
Rising Republic of Ireland star Jack Moylan scored twice in the first half, winning and converting an 11th-minute penalty and then picking his spot to beat Federico Ravaglia in a one-on one in the 35th.

Hornets skipper Mattie Pollock had brought down Moylan for the penalty and then headed into his own net from a corner in the 41st minute before Ollie Tanner added the fourth in the fifth minute of first-half added time.

Having lost to bottom of the table Burnley 4-0 at home last weekend, with all the goals coming in the first half, it was another slap in the face for the 500 travelling Hornets fans who once again expressed their discontent with the owners and the manager.

Alessio Dionisi signed a two-year deal to manage Watford in June when he became their 12th manager, excluding interim appointments, to take charge of the club since the end of the 2020-21 season under Gino Pozzo's ownership.

This was a fourth defeat in a row and the sixth in the last seven games. With Burnley continuing their revival with a draw at home against Charlton it meant Dionisi's side slipped to 22nd in the table while the Bluebirds flew up to 18th.

Last weekend the Watford faithful started chanting "Sack the board" at Vicarage Road and there were boos all round for the manager and his players at the end of their latest humiliation.

For Cardiff it was only their second win of the season and it could have been by even more goals, though Watford had the first clear-cut chance of the game when Myron Boadu ran onto a poor back-pass by Dylan Lawlor but failed to beat Nathan Trott in the home goal.

Moylan's brace turned the game in favour of Cardiff, who were ruthless throughout.

After their dominant first half, Chris Willock won a second penalty in the 64th minute and - with Moylan still on the pitch and on a hat-trick - picked himself up and saw his spot-kick saved by Ravaglia.

The Watford keeper could not stop substitute Callum Robinson from adding a fifth goal in the 85th minute.

Hector Kyprianou headed home a consolation goal two minutes later, although not even that could stop the boos at the final whistle from the Watford fans.

"It was a difficult weekend for us because it's such a long build-up during the international break. We wanted to play well and win on Saturday but it wasn't good, so to bounce back in the fashion we did tonight was hugely satisfying.

"We know Watford have problems, but you've still got to beat what's in front of you. We felt miserable on Saturday and now we just need to build some momentum.

"We are aware of the challenge we face at Middlesbrough on Saturday but it's a challenge that we want and we're looking forward to."

"I asked for a reaction after the Burnley defeat but I didn't get one. I was very angry with my players.

"The game was gone by half-time and I decided to give them 10 more minutes to see if they could turn things around in the second half.

"They couldn't and that's why I made five substitutions. It is now important to take responsibility for where we are, for me as the coach and for the players.

"I didn't like what I saw tonight. There was no reaction on the pitch after just one negative moment. We have to solve these problems together because there isn't one player or one person who can solve them.

"I want to continue with my responsibilities and to work with my players because I think together we can arrive with a good result. I speak with my owner every day and I have a good relationship with him, but this is football and I know that last season Watford changed four coaches."

articles.title: Wolves 1-3 Bolton: Cesar Peixoto's side fall to first home Championship defeat of the season
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Wolves and Bolton at Molineux on Tuesday; Atsuki Ito, Sam Dalby and Josh Sheehan score to inflict a first home league defeat on Cesar Peixoto's men
articles.body:
Atsuki Ito gave Steven Schumacher's visitors a deserved 28th-minute lead and although Jean-Ricner Bellegarde equalised five minutes after the break, substitute Sam Dalby and Josh Sheehan struck in the last 20 minutes to secure back-to-back away wins for Bolton.

Samuel Iling-Junior missed a one-on-one chance to put the away side ahead in the 11th minute.

Sheehan split the Wolves defence to put the on-loan Aston Villa winger clean through with only Jose Sa to beat.

But the Portuguese goalkeeper was perfectly placed to block Iling-Junior's low shot and the loose ball was cleared.

Bolton had another chance to take the lead but Sheehan's deflected drive from the edge of the box drew a superb diving save from Sa to his right.

Mateus Mane had Wolves' first chance and he went within a whisker of the far post with a curling effort just wide.

Bolton took the lead when Sa appeared to flap at Sheehan's cross from Iling-Junior's short corner and although Ladislav Krejci nodded clear, Ito fired home from 10 yards.

Wolves were starting to come more into the game and the unmarked Fer Lopez headed straight at goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu from Hugo Bueno's cross.

Bueno was next to try his luck with a curling effort from 22 yards that just spun wide, away from the far post at the last moment.

Wolves brought themselves level in the 50th minute.

Bellegarde controlled Krejci's long diagonal pass and held off Akin Famewo before firing a low shot into the far bottom corner of the net.

Krejci glanced just over from Kieran Trippier's free-kick as Wolves continued to press.

Mane curled inches over the bar from 25 yards and Adam Armstrong flashed an effort into the sidenetting from Jordan James' cross as the hosts probed for a second goal.

Armstrong then somehow hit Bazunu from point-blank range from substitute Rafiki Said's cross.

But completely against the run of play, Bolton regained the lead in the 72nd minute.

Gaizka Larrazabal crossed after a one-two with Ethan Erhahon and Dalby finished at the near post.

Lopez ballooned a shot over the crossbar as Wolves desperately tried to find an equaliser.

But instead the next goal came from the visitors in the 82nd minute when Sheehan capped a fine performance with a looping shot into the top corner from 20 yards that Sa could not get to.

"The 3-1 scoreline is an unfair result because we created a lot of chances.

"We deserved more because we were the better team. The team showed effort, courage and commitment all of the game but sometimes this happens in football.

"I am responsible for the result. The players and I have to do better.

"We have to be more clinical from the edge of the box and with the last cross or last pass.

"We have to win the duels inside the box but we dominated the game.

"I'd be more worried if we weren't putting the ball in the box, but inside of the box we can do better."

"It's right up there because they were a Premier League team last season.

"It was a really good result and a really important one. The players should be really proud of their work.

"It was a really good performance and it needed to be. They are a top team, it's a really difficult place to come so we needed everyone to play to the best of their ability and the energy to be at the top level.

"On Saturday (a 2-1 home defeat to Stoke City) we didn't perform as well as we can but tonight was excellent against a really good opponent."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Birmingham 4-0 Preston: August Priske scores twice as Blues thump Graham Alexander's struggling North End
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Birmingham and Preston at St Andrew's on Tuesday; August Priske scores twice and Liam Millar and Demarai Gray strike as Chris Davies' Blues secured a thumping win
articles.body:
Two goals from August Priske and one each for Liam Millar and Demarai Gray gave Chris Davies' men a third win in four games - and their first at home.

Preston, who played most of the second half with 10 men, remain rooted to the bottom of the table with just one victory after 10 matches.

Birmingham took the lead in the 33th minute when they cut the visitors wide open down the right as a first time, round-the-corner pass from Jay Stansfield freed Patrick Roberts.

The winger had time and space to roll a cross along the edge of the six-yard box for Millar to stroke home his second Blues goal.

The hosts then put the game out of reach with two goals in two first-half stoppage-time minutes.

Preston nodded off when referee Sam Allison dropped an uncontested ball at Alex Cochrane's feet and the left-back immediately curled a pass behind the defence for Priske to side-foot home in the second minute of added time.

Seconds later Jhon Solis dispossessed Jordan Thompson as North End tried to play out and poked the ball to Stansfield, who squared for Priske to curl home via a post from the edge of the box.

The Dane came close to a hat-trick soon after the restart when Millar sent over a dangerous cross from the left which Priske nodded goalwards from 12 yards, but too close to Daniel Iversen.

North End's plight became even worse 11 minutes after the restart when, having been booked at the start of the second half for a foul on Millar, Stan Mills lunged in on Cochrane and was shown a second yellow card.

Max Bird almost scored just a minute after coming on when Bright Osayi-Samuel's right-wing centre was headed up, but only as far as the penalty spot where the midfielder volleyed straight at the goalkeeper.

The former Bristol City man should have made it four with a quarter of an hour to go when Roberts picked him out from the right, but Bird could only head at Iversen.

The fourth did arrive in the 77th minute when Taylor Gardner-Hickman strode forward, laid off for Bird near the area, who in turn found Gray in the left side of the area. The Jamaica international checked inside and curled home his third of the season.

"I think he [Priske] has been great, what I always say is the first thing I ask of them is to do all the ugly bits of the game; the duels, the fighting, the scrapping and the running, the pressing and all that - which he will do.

"That's the only way he's going to play if he does that every game, but for number nines it's goals they live off and I know he's going to score goals because I've always said when you see it in training, with the technical side of their game, you can always see a finisher.

"He's got two good feet, makes good contact with the ball, has a good touch and can score headers because he's got the leap and the size."

"I'm hurt, obviously, the scoreline, the way the last five minutes of the first half went was a major blow.

"We were well in the game, I thought, we had opportunities in the first half, at 1-0 I still think there was a game there for us to win.

"But at 3-0 and the manner of the goals and the timing of the goals, it just takes the wind out of you.

"We were looking for a mentality in the second half, which I believe we got, but it became extremely difficult when we went down to 10."

Alexander was not too critical of Mills, adding: "If you've been booked away from home, a vociferous crowd, you stay on your feet after that and don't hurt your team. But he's a young player, we all make mistakes, his heart's in the right place."

articles.title: Republic of Ireland 4-0 Kazakhstan (agg 12-0): We have to 'lock in' for World Cup dream - Katie McCabe
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland captain Katie McCabe is already focused on the final World Cup play-off with Poland after a big win over Kazakhstan.
articles.body:
The final whistle had just blown in Cork, but Katie McCabe's mind was already six weeks ahead.

Eight goals to the good from Friday, the second leg of the Women's World Cup play-off with Kazakhstan was always going to be an easy night for the Republic of Ireland.

There were another four goals on the night, including a powerful strike from McCabe, and it leaves Carla Ward's side just two matches away from the 2027 Women's World Cup.

Poland are the team that stands in their way of making back-to-back finals, and McCabe knows her players will have to rise to the task.

"Two games and we're going to Brazil, but full focus over the next six weeks," the 31-year-old told RTE Sport.

Republic of Ireland ease into World Cup play-off final with Poland

After thrashing Kazakhstan in the first leg, Ward had wanted to build momentum and captain McCabe was brought back into the starting team after serving a one-game suspension in Astana.

After a shock 4-0 home defeat by Slovenia in Ward's second game in charge in February 2025, the Republic of Ireland have soared from strength to strength.

They beat Belgium in a promotion/relegation play-off to win promotion to League A of the Nations League, and defeated the Netherlands and twice beat play-off opponents Poland to stay in the top tier going forward.

"We've put ourselves in a really good position. The opponents we've faced, top-10 opponents, the girls have done brilliantly.

"Once Carla came in it's a transition period and it takes a bit of time to find our feet.

"We learnt our lesson with that heavy defeat by Slovenia two years ago and we've built and grown. We've tried to gather as much momentum as possible."

While Poland, who defeated Belgium on penalties after a 3-3 draw over the two legs, are a dangerous side - largely thanks for Barcelona striker Ewa Pajor, they lost both games against the Irish during qualifying in April.

"For us, we've played both teams recently and it's going to be different come November.

"We know there's a World Cup place at stake so we need to be ready. It's an exciting one."

McCabe says her summer move to Chelsea, which came after her contract at Arsenal came to an end, has been a "breath of fresh air" and can only help her at club and country.

"The time had come for me to start a new chapter. Ever since I've come in to work with Sonia [Bompastor, Chelsea manager] and the girls it has been brilliant.

"I'm enjoying my football again and I'm just taking it game-by-game, but for me the most important thing is being in the best position to qualify for the World Cup."

McCabe added that the Irish players know what it takes to reach the biggest tournament in the sport, after achieving the feat for the first time in Australia in 2023.

"We've had some highs and lows over the years. It's going to be really important and we'll stick together going into November.

"We'll be doing everything we can to get over the line and get this country to the World Cup again."

articles.title: Iñigo Pérez: “Ganar con el plan de partido tiene un valor incalculable para reforzar las ideas”
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Villarreal destaca la reacción de su equipo tras el 0-1 del Nápoles, reivindica la fidelidad al modelo de juego y pide pasar página de inmediato para centrarse en el Elche.
articles.summary: El técnico del Villarreal destaca la reacción de su equipo tras el 0-1 del Nápoles, reivindica la fidelidad al modelo de juego y pide pasar página de inmediato para centrarse en el Elche.
articles.body: Iñigo Pérez valoró la victoria por 3-1 del Villarreal ante el Nápoles como una demostración de madurez competitiva y convicción en el modelo de juego. El técnico amarillo destacó la capacidad de su equipo para no desviarse del plan pese a comenzar por detrás en el marcador, aseguró que triunfos como este fortalecen la fe colectiva en la propuesta futbolística y rebajó cualquier lectura de futuro en la Champions, insistiendo en que el único foco inmediato está puesto en el próximo compromiso liguero frente al Elche. La remontada del Villarreal frente al Nápoles dejó especialmente satisfecho a Iñigo Pérez por la forma en la que se produjo. El entrenador consideró que el aspecto decisivo no fue el resultado final, sino la capacidad de sus jugadores para mantenerse fieles a la estrategia diseñada pese al golpe inicial del tanto italiano. “Tenemos que intentar que esa visión de que nos hagan un gol no se vea como un pozo sino como algo aceptado, que es algo que puede ocurrir. Ha sido clave no despegarnos de la estrategia ni de la táctica y así llegó la victoria”. Para el técnico, un encuentro como el de este martes supone un impulso extraordinario para consolidar la identidad que pretende construir desde su llegada al banquillo. Pérez aseguró que los resultados favorables permiten reforzar mensajes que ya existían dentro del vestuario, aunque muchas veces quedan eclipsados cuando la pelota no entra: “Todas las victorias aumentan la fe y las ideas del equipo y de un entrenador. Cuando ganas y el equipo ha desarrollado un plan de partido, eso tiene un valor incalculable para aumentar esa demanda. Es justo decir que los jugadores vienen haciéndolo desde el minuto uno que estoy aquí, pero cuando los resultados no son favorables no puedes venir aquí a decirlo”. El preparador castellonense también rechazó cualquier comparación con campañas anteriores en competición continental. Recordó que su experiencia en Europa le enseñó la enorme exigencia táctica que requieren estos encuentros, aunque insistió en que el pasado no debe servir de referencia para analizar el presente del equipo. “Los partidos europeos requieren de un análisis táctico muy profundo y en la Champions sabemos que cada partido es una final. Lo ocurrido el año pasado no me concierne. Son años y proyectos diferentes”. Pese al prestigio del triunfo y a la ilusión que genera el recorrido continental, Pérez quiso rebajar la euforia y dirigir toda la atención hacia el siguiente compromiso de Liga. El entrenador dejó claro que la victoria sobre el conjunto italiano no tendrá influencia alguna cuando lleguen futuras citas europeas de máxima exigencia. “Ahora viene un periodo corto de disfrute y a partir de mañana a pensar en el Elche. Ahí está el foco. Luego ya vendrá la Champions. Lo que ha sucedido hoy no va a supeditar lo que pase contra el PSG o el Liverpool. Cuando juguemos en Anfield ni nos vamos a acordar de lo de hoy”. Además, se refirió brevemente a la sanción de un minuto impuesta a su equipo por una pérdida de tiempo, evitando la polémica y apostando por adaptarse a la normativa. “Las normas que se establecen o van variando debemos aceptarlas y estar más espabilados para que no vuelva a suceder, porque era una desventaja muy grande”. Por último, mostró su apoyo al guardameta Gulacsi tras el reciente episodio sufrido fuera de los terrenos de juego, aunque prefirió mantener el asunto en el ámbito privado. “Lo primero que haces cuando te lo dicen es imaginarte lo que hubiera sido en cada uno de nosotros. La empatía con él es máxima, no puede ser de otro modo. Pero es su vida privada”. Proporcione sus comentarios sobre BizChat

articles.title: El Manchester United vuelve a implosionar: "Fuimos lamentables"
articles.standfirst: Lisandro Martínez apunta a los despachos tras la derrota ante el Atlético en el Metropolitano
articles.summary: Lisandro Martínez apunta a los despachos tras la derrota ante el Atlético en el Metropolitano
articles.body: Quitando el 4-0 ante el Sabah, debutante en Champions, el Manchester United no celebra una victoria desde agosto. Una temporada más, y ya son demasiadas, los Red Devils se han empadronado en uno de los últimos círculos del infierno y no son capaces de encontrar una escalera que les saque de las profundidades. Decimoterceros en Premier, con una victoria (la del 30 de agosto ante el Ipswich) y seis puntos en seis jornadas, los de Carrick ya escuchan por costumbre las críticas que, precisamente y como es habitual, apuntan a su técnico. "No se puede estar cambiando, cambiando y cambiando de entrenador. ¿Qué pasa con otras áreas? Esta noche es fácil hablar del entrenador, es fácil hablar de los jugadores, pero también tenemos que fijarnos en otros aspectos", dijo Lisandro Martínez, muy cabreado tras la derrota ante el Atlético de Madrid, apuntando a los despachos de Old Trafford. "Hemos hecho un partido realmente pobre. Realmente pobre. Tengo que controlarme mucho, pero a veces es un reflejo de cómo está nuestro club en este momento", expresó Lisandro en Amazon Prime tras el duelo del Metropolitano y apuntando directamente a Jason Wilcox, director de fútbol del United: "Espero más inversión. Al 100%. Espero más de nuestro director técnico. Tengo que ser honesto, como jugadores tenemos que hacer más, pero también es importante, cuando tienes un equipo fuerte, estar preparado para una noche como esta". "Tuvimos una temporada fantástica el año pasado y ahora esperamos más de la directiva, de los altos mandos, para que traigan más jugadores para competir, porque muchos equipos también han fichado a muchos jugadores", continuó. En Movistar, en español, dejó otra frase contundente: "Fuera roja o no, no se puede hacer nada. Me quedo con el rendimiento de nuestro equipo, que fue lamentable". El Manchester United no fue capaz de pasar del empate ante el Tottenham (1-1) en el primer partido tras el parón, encadenando así su cuarto partido seguido en Premier sin ganar (2-2 ante el Everton, 0-1 contra el City y 1-1 frente al Fulham). La derrota en el Metropolitano no hace más que agravar una situación en la que Carrick ya está en entredicho. "A todos nos importa la situación y lo demostramos de diferentes maneras, pero ahora es el momento de estar juntos y superarlo", dijo el técnico inglés. No todo el mundo fue tan crítico con el equipo como Lisandro. Wayne Rooney le dio un pequeño tirón de orejas al argentino. "Creo que tal vez se ha excedido un poco, y eso debería haberse quedado en el ámbito privado", comentó en la retransmisión y aseguró que quizás el futbolista ya tenía pensado soltar ese discurso fuese como fuese el encuentro: "En cierto modo tiene razón en cuanto a que el club necesita invertir más en la parte delantera del campo y en la defensa, pero creo que parece que tenía una agenda y quería decir eso porque no refleja el rendimiento que yo pensé que había sido mejor". "También es una falta de respeto hacia sus compañeros. Les está diciendo que no son lo suficientemente buenos", insistió Rooney. Paul Robinson, ex portero de Inglaterra, se expresó en BBC Radio 5 Live en los mismos términos... aunque acabó dando la razón al jugador: "Cuestiono el momento elegido, con todo el revuelo que hay actualmente en torno al Manchester United; es necesario que salga una actitud positiva del vestuario, pero es evidente que no han fichado bien, que necesitan más jugadores y que la plantilla no es lo suficientemente fuerte". El United visita al Leeds el domingo a las 15.00 (hora peninsular española). Y necesita una victoria para olvidar estos episodios y remontar el vuelo aunque haya quien, como el comentarista de SkySports Clinton Morrison, no lo tengan claro: "El Leeds parte como favorito para el domingo"

articles.title: Allegri: "En los partidos de máximo nivel se notan más los errores"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador italiano cree que "nos falta encontrar un equilibrio"
articles.summary: El entrenador italiano cree que "nos falta encontrar un equilibrio"
articles.body: El entrenador del Nápoles, Massimiliano Allegri, afirmó este martes, tras la derrota de su equipo ante el Villarreal (3-1), que a su equipo le falto "encontrar un equilibrio en el juego" y admitió que les "faltó algo más" para obtener un resultado positivo. El técnico trasalpino recordó que el nivel de la Liga de Campeones "es muy alto" y disculpó a Politano por el error en el primer gol del Villarreal, pero no que su equipo de descentrara tras el empate. "El error puede pasar, un equipo fuerte como el Nápoles tiene que estar tranquilo y seguir jugando", dijo Allegri, que reiteró que es necesario encontrar "un equilibrio para afrontar los partidos de forma diferente". El italiano aseguró que su equipo para mejorar debe conceder "menos disparos a portería" y reiteró que en partidos del máximo nivel "se notan más los errores". Allegri también se refirió al planteamiento táctico y fue crítico al reconocer que el Nápoles con balón "debe mejorar".

articles.title: Carrick: "No creo que fuera roja, no estoy de acuerdo con esa decisión"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del United cree que la expulsión fue la puntilla para la derrota
articles.summary: El entrenador del United cree que la expulsión fue la puntilla para la derrota
articles.body: Michael Carrick, entrenador del Manchester United, lamentó la derrota de su equipo ante el Atlético y mostró su malestar por la expulsión de Leny Yoro tras una acción con Jonathan David en el minuto 74. Tarjeta roja: "No creo que sea, no estoy de acuerdo con esa decisión, no iba a velocidad y es un empujón muy suave. Empezamos mal el partido y se nos puso más cuesta arriba. Tuvimos dos para empatar, pudimos mejorar con el avance del partido, pero esa tarjeta tuvo una gran repercusión". Falta de confianza de los delanteros: "No, pueden fallar goles, no es una cuestión individual, hay que seguir creándolas y defender mejor. Después del 1-0 lo interpretamos mejor". Lisandro dice que faltó inversión este verano: "No he visto la entrevista, pero esto son las emociones del partido, la decepción, no es el momento de hablar de estas cosas. Lo importante es que a partir de aquí nos levantemos". Animado por Lisandro: "No pongo en duda su querer ganar. Con estos resultados, luego habrá algo que no va bien, pero hay voluntad de seguir trabajando". Palabras duras: "Tengo que ver la entrevista para hablar de ello". Charla técnica: "Hemos respondido bastante bien al gol temprano, controlamos algunas fases, sabíamos que era un partido difícil y aún así tuvimos varios unos contra uno con el portero. Hicimos bastantes cosas bien, también dejamos espacios". Sentimiento de que todo está en contra: "Las voces se están escuchando, hay pasión por hacerlo bien, trabajar y mejorar. Hay positividad, hoy no pudimos, pero era complicado. Y encajar tan pronto nos hizo ir al tran tran todo el rato. Este fin de semana es una buena ocasión para remar todos en la misma dirección"

articles.title: Man City vs PSG: Champions League – teams, predictions, line ups
articles.summary: Man City host PSG in their first UCL match since being found guilty of serious Premier League financial breaches.
articles.body:
Who : Manchester City vs Paris Saint-Germain What : UEFA Champions League , matchday 2 Where : City of Manchester Stadium, Manchester, United Kingdom When: Wednesday, October 14, at 8pm (19:00 GMT) How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live updates from 16:00 GMT.

After being found guilty of an unprecedented breach of the Premier League’s financial rules, Manchester City turn their focus to the Champions League this week, as they host two-time holders PSG on matchday two.

Fresh off a defiant league win over Liverpool at a hostile Anfield , City have momentum on their side as they welcome PSG in a clash of two of Europe’s finest teams.

Fans will have a golden opportunity to witness a mouthwatering battle between Erling Haaland, City’s lethal striker, and forward Ferran Torres, who is enjoying his new spell at PSG after helping Spain win the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Haaland has eight goals across all competitions; Torres has seven. On Wednesday, more could be added to those tallies in this round of the UCL.

After Tuesday’s league matches, PSG are ranked fifth while Man City are ninth.

Here’s everything to know about the clash:

Which financial rules have Man City breached?

An independent commission found City guilty of almost all of the 115 charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, as well as three of four charges relating to failures to cooperate with the investigation.

City have denied wrongdoing and lodged an appeal .

No sanctions have been decided yet, but if City’s appeal fails, potential punishments include a significant point deduction and expulsion from the Premier League.

There is even the prospect of three Premier League titles being stripped from City, who won them from 2009 to 2018, the period to which the charges relate.

Man City have maintained a perfect record in the Premier League, winning all six matches.

Their only defeat across all competitions this season came in mid-August, when they lost to Arsenal in the Community Shield, the traditional curtain-raiser to the English football season.

PSG, who usually dominate Ligue 1 having won a record 14 titles, are fifth in the table, three points adrift of leaders Barcelona.

What happened in the first round of Champions League matches?

Reigning champions PSG thrashed Slovan Bratislava 6-1 at home in their first UCL match of the season, while Man City won 2-0 away to Porto in their campaign opener.

That keeps PSG fifth and Man City ninth in the league phase of this year’s Champions League.

The top eight teams at the end of the league phase qualify directly to the knockout rounds, which begin with the round of 16.

The Opta supercomputer has made City the favourites, with a win probability of 44.1 percent. PSG were given a 32 percent chance of winning, while a draw was estimated at a 23.9 percent likelihood.

(Last five matches across all competitions, latest match first)

Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki (Man City): Haaland’s six goals make him the Premier League’s leading scorer this season. His excellent form follows an equally impressive World Cup debut with Norway in North America. Haaland’s teammate Cherki is another vital City attacker with five goals and two assists in all competitions.

Ferran Torres and Marquinhos (PSG): Torres, whose extra-time goal guided Spain to the 2026 World Cup triumph, has made a quick start to life at his new club PSG, scoring seven goals in all competitions. That includes a hat-trick in PSG’s first UCL fixture. Meanwhile, captain Marquinhos has been an important presence in defence and has also scored three times.

City are unbeaten at home against PSG (W3 D1), winning each of the last three games – most recently 2-1 on matchday 5 in 2021-22.

City also defeated PSG in the 2015-16 quarterfinals (2-2 away, 1-0 home) and the 2020-21 semifinals (2-1 away, 2-0 home).

City have lost only two of their last eight matches against French opponents (W5 D1), although they have won only one of their last four (D1 L2), drawing 2-2 at Monaco on Matchday 2 last season.

PSG are unbeaten in their last 11 matches against English teams (W8 D3), beating Aston Villa 2-1 in August’s UEFA Super Cup. Last season’s Champions League final against Arsenal is the only fixture in the last six they did not win in normal time.

A 2-0 victory at Liverpool in last season’s quarterfinal second leg was PSG’s third in succession in England.

City have a fully fit squad for the match.

Gianluigi Donnarumma; Matheus Nunes, Marc Guehi, Ruben Dias, Josko Gvardiol; Ayyoub Bouaddi, Enzo Fernandez; Phil Foden, Rayan Cherki, Antoine Semenyo; Erling Haaland

Senny Mayulu is out until late October with a thigh injury.

articles.title: Ji-sung Eom: Swansea City winger the target of alleged racism at Millwall
articles.summary: Swansea City head coach Vitor Matos says the lengthy stoppage during their 1-0 win away at Millwall was a result of racist abuse aimed at winger Ji-sung Eom.
articles.body:
Swansea City head coach Vitor Matos says the lengthy stoppage during their 1-0 win away at Millwall was a result of racist abuse aimed at Ji-sung Eom.

The South Korea winger was among the Swansea substitutes, and had been warming up on the side of the pitch when the Championship game was brought to a halt.

Referee Edward Duckworth had lengthy discussions with both sets of coaches, during which the game was paused for around seven minutes.

Following the stoppage, an announcement was made over the speakers at The Den confirming there had been alleged chants of racism and that police were working to identify any offenders using CCTV.

Speaking after the game, Matos said it was the 24-year-old who had been the subject of the abuse.

"The situation was with Ji-sung Eom," said Matos.

"The referee followed the protocol for these sort of situations, they did the right thing. Millwall also did the right thing to get the protocol moving on.

"We all know there is no space for this, this kind of situation should not happen.

"When they do happen we are here to stand with the player, in this case it is our player."

The incident marred what was otherwise an evening of celebration for the Swans, as Ronald's late strike sealed a 1-0 win for the league leaders.

Millwall stated they were "aware of an alleged, individual incident of discriminatory abuse towards a Swansea City player during the second half" of the game.

"The club operates a zero-tolerance policy towards any form of discriminatory abuse. Any individual found to have engaged in such behaviour will face the strongest possible action," added the hosts.

"The club is working alongside the relevant authorities to establish the facts and is unable to comment further as tonight's alleged incident is the subject of an ongoing police investigation, which the club fully supports."

Victory kept Swansea two points clear at the top of the Championship, with the Welsh club putting together their best start to a season in a century.

Matos said he was saddened by the abuse aimed at Eom, but says the rest of the squad will rally around their team-mate.

"He is a smart kid, he is not happy with the situation but he knows we will stay with him and follow the situation as long as we can," added Matos.

"Millwall did the right thing by announcing there is no place for this sort of thing.

"I'm happy with how it was handled, but really sad that it happened. Now it is about evaluating the situation and we'll see what happens."

articles.title: Man Utd defender Lisandro Martinez extraordinarily calls out club's hierarchy after Atletico Madrid loss in Champions League
articles.summary: Man Utd's Lisandro Martinez astonishingly attacks club's hierarchy after Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid; Martinez told Amazon Prime: "We expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete"; he added: "I expect more from our technical director"
articles.body:
In an astonishing post-match interview, the Argentina international criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad.

The defender said he had expected more from "upstairs", singling out technical director Jason Wilcox, in the most recent transfer window in which they failed to improve their options at left-back and up front.

Man Utd spent £155m on just four major summer signings after a third-place Premier League finish last season, which earned a return to the Champions League for the first time in three years.

"I have to control myself a lot, but sometimes it's a reflection of how our club is at the moment," Martinez told Amazon Prime .

"We had a fantastic season last season, and now we expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete because many teams have brought in many players as well."

Asked whether he had expected more investment in the squad in summer, Martinez said: "Yes, 100 per cent.

"I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest. And also, as a player, we have to do more.

"It's also important to build a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

Tuesday's loss in Madrid extended Man Utd's winless run to five games, piling pressure on boss Michael Carrick.

"He does his best," he said of Carrick. "But every season is different. You can't stay with what you did last season.

"The teams know how you play, they know every detail. If you don't change, next season is a big problem."

Asked about Carrick's future, Martinez replied: "You start changing, changing, changing managers. But what about [moves his eyes upwards] other areas?"

Martinez looked up and then shrugged, saying, "I can't say more" before deciding to add a final dig.

"Because also tonight it is easy to say the coach, it is easy to say the players, but also we have to see other areas," he said, pointing up and nodding.

Carrick and Tielemans asked about Martinez comments

It was a jaw-dropping interview that Youri Tielemans, one of three outfield summer signings, refused to comment on, while Martinez's outburst dominated the post-match press conference with Carrick.

Asked if he agreed with Martinez's view, he said: "Well, I haven't seen the interview. I've half heard about it in the other interviews I've done.

"I think it's a little bit on the emotions of the game as well, coming here and being disappointed not to get something from the game.

"Straight after a game for me is not the time to talk about that interview because I haven't seen it, so I can't really comment on that.

"But I think it's important for us to move forward quickly, really. I think there's a big game on Sunday, and it's really important that we move forward and we stay focused on that.

"There's disappointment within the group. I'm bitterly disappointed in certain things, and the boys are as well as a group."

Rooney heavily criticises Martinez outburst

Manchester United's all-time leading scorer Wayne Rooney speaking to Amazon Prime :

"It's a difficult one because I always used to think I was outspoken as a player and you want to have your opinion.

"I think he has maybe gone a bit too far. That's for the manager, and that should really stay internal.

"The fans want to hear the players speak; they want to hear the players care, so you can clearly see he cares and he wants the team to invest more money, and more players, and to do that he is probably one of the players who is out the door through his performances. His performances haven't been good enough.

"But I think in some ways he is right in terms of the club needs to invest more, at the top end of the pitch and in defence as well.

"But it looks like that was a bit of an agenda; he's wanted to say that, because that doesn't mirror the performance. I thought the performance was better.

"It's a bit disrespectful to his team-mates as well. He is disrespecting his team-mates because he's saying the team isn't good enough.

"Bruno (Fernandes) is the only one who has any right to come out and say anything like that as captain. And even then it should be behind closed doors if there are issues, which does happen.

"Players have conversations with the manager, the manager has conversations with the board, but that interview is not going to help the situation the club are in at the minute.

"That's going to bring a greater noise around it; the players are not happy, they're not settled, they don't trust in their team-mates. That's not going to help at all."

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher speaking to CBS Sports:

"Doesn't do anybody any good at all, and they will be the story now for the next few days, all about this.

"Now, as supporters, every set of supporters don't like the suits or the guys upstairs, so United fans will lap this up and think it's great. I think it's awful that he's come out and said that right now. I do.

"And when he's saying 'we had a fantastic season last season', they didn't. A manager got sacked last season. They finished third because they had no cup games. They weren't in Europe. They got knocked out of the cup competitions very early.

"The reason they finished third is that Liverpool and Chelsea were that bad as well. Now we're seeing the real Manchester United this season."

Analysis: Martinez unlikley to last long at Man Utd

Everyone has heard a Manchester United fan voicing the criticisms made by Lisandro Martinez in Madrid. It is another thing entirely to see a player doing it.

Many of those fans will see Martinez's comments as a necessary intervention to address an issue which long pre-dates INEOS' involvement at Old Trafford but has certainly not been helped by Sir Jim Ratcliffe's minority investment.

Others, like Wayne Rooney, will question the player's motives. Martinez has entered the final year of his contract and cannot claim to have done enough to have earned another. Perhaps he has been told as much. Players who speak out publicly like this do not tend to last long.

Cristiano Ronaldo called out the Glazers in 2022 in his famous Piers Morgan interview and left United within a week. Martinez's compatriot Cristian Romero criticised Spurs' hierarchy in January in an Instagram post and was gone by the summer.

Irrespective of Martinez's motivation, it is hard to argue with his point. United set Carrick up for a fall by failing to sign a left-back or a striker over the summer. The midfield rebuild that was hyped up for many months before the summer has not lived up to expectation either.

It is hard to understand quite what the plan is at United looking back at the last few years. United have had three managers in that window of time. Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick. All with different approaches that bear little resemblance to the other.

Martinez's comments will not help Carrick. But given the sense of hopelessness that has engulfed the fanbase, you can understand why some will welcome his comments. Martinez is right in saying United's issues stretch far beyond the manager.

Steve: Martinez is 100 per cent right. The board are an absolute disgrace; the biggest club in the world and yet they persist with the same defenders we've had for five years. Teams know our weaknesses; the board have once again let the manager down badly.

Jonesy: I don't agree with Martinez. They had money, but spent it on players like Andrey Santos who can't get in the Chelsea team - what makes him good enough for Utd? I saw professional players unable to execute simple passes, and lapses of concentration in defence, again. Not good enough!

Date D: You can change the manager as much as you want, but when the hierarchy stays the same, you get the same results. Well done, Martinez!

Ciara : For once, a Man Utd player coming out to call out hierarchy. What a legend.

Dantoken : I stand with him. Nothing changes until changes are made at the top of the club.

Garbs : Agree with Martinez, squad should be bigger and more quality. The main issues are with those above off the pitch.

articles.title: Lexi Potter: England Women midfielder the present, not just the future after impressive debut in World Cup play-off
articles.summary: Lexi Potter made her England debut against Greece in the World Cup play-off second leg at the King Power; the 20-year-old Chelsea midfielder impressed and could be in line to start if the Lionesses reach the Brazil tournament next summer
articles.body:
It's a big shout for a player that's only just broken into the England team, but her 60-minute debut against Greece couldn't have gone much better.

"It was really special," the Chelsea midfielder told ITV Sport after the game. "I am very happy and proud. It was a bit of a rush before the game and I lost my phone! I was a bit nervous but once I got on the pitch, I really enjoyed it.

"It was almost a dream come true. As a young girl, it's what you dream of, playing for your country. To make my debut and to be able to start as well is very special."

The 20-year old grew into the game at the King Power Stadium. She broke up attacks, showed her range of passing, allowed Keira Walsh, Georgia Stanway and Lauren James to shine and even had a goal disallowed.

England's next few games get gradually harder. Ukraine await in the final round of play-offs before a Nations League campaign against three teams in and around the top 20 in the world.

Potter, if trusted, can get a chance to grow into the role as an England starter while also playing in important matches.

Not many players make their debut in their first international camp under Sarina Wiegman. The fact Potter was picked to start a game shows how much she's impressing already.

"You could see that there were some nerves but that's completely normal," Wiegman told ITV Sport of her midfielder after the game in Leicester. "We kept an eye on her already and now she's a starter for Chelsea, she did really well.

"In our camp, she did really well straight away. Your first start for England, that's a big moment, but you can tell the position she picks up [that she was ready]. She scored a goal that was unfortunately disallowed, but nice for her."

Keira Walsh, Potter's team-mate at Chelsea, has also become her biggest hype artist. She's been telling anyone that'll listen about the midfielder's quality and potential.

Now the Lionesses have seen it first-hand on the training pitch and in a competitive match.

England can take 26 players to the World Cup, a first in the women's tournament. That means six or seven midfielders will be part of the squad.

With Walsh and Stanway certainties, it's a battle between Potter, Laura Blinkilde Brown, Erica Meg Parkinson, Ella Toone, Grace Clinton and Lucia Kendall for the other spots.

It's realistic one or two of them could be left behind. Toone and Clinton were on the outside looking in at the start of the international break before being called up as injury replacements.

All of a sudden England have a load of options in a position they were once struggling for depth.

Georgia Stanway to Sky Sports News : "She's a really good kid. It's so good to have her around the group. She's composed, she's calm and she appears older than what you think she is. She's come in and it's as if she's been here for a really long time."

Freya Godfrey - who also made her England debut on Tuesday - to Sky Sports News: "I can't even explain it. We were in our hotel room earlier and we were going through our camera rolls with Erica [Meg Parkinson] and I came across a picture of me and Lex from 2022 on camp.

"To then have this night with her, I couldn't be prouder of her and the season she's had. She more than deserves it. To share it with someone as special as her, I've grown up with her in the youth age groups, and talking about it gives me chills.

"Watching her walk out and sing the national anthem, me and Erica felt really emotional and proud of her."

Jess Carter to Sky Sports News : "She's great. I remember playing with her when I was at Chelsea. It's great to see her here and in this camp, she's been excellent. She's professional and she definitely does not stand out as if she's fresh in here so I'm really happy for her."

Alessia Russo to ITV Sport : "She's been brilliant in training. You can tell that she's ready for this level. She is a great kid and wants to learn. She's got the best in learning off Keira. She looks so confident and composed."

articles.title: Manchester United’s Martinez blasts board’s lack of investment
articles.summary: Manchester United beaten 2-0 at Atletico Madrid, but defender Lisandro Martinez slams club’s failure to invest in team.
articles.body:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez blasted the club’s board for a perceived lack of investment this summer, after the team were beaten by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday.

United are winless in five games across all competitions after the 2-0 defeat in the Spanish capital and have made their worst start to a league season in 40 years.

“Really poor,” Martinez told Amazon Prime when asked about the team’s performance against Atletico.

“I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection… [or] mirror of how our club is at the moment.”

Martinez said he “100 percent” expected more investment in the squad over the summer after United finished third in the Premier League last season and returned to Europe’s top competition.

“I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox], I have to be honest, as players we have to do more, but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for these kind of nights,” he continued.

Martinez said last season the club had “created the base to create an amazing team”, but they did not follow through.

Pressure is mounting on coach Michael Carrick after five games without a win, but Martinez suggested sacking the Englishman was not the way forward.

“You can’t keep changing, changing, changing the manager. What about other areas? I can’t say more,” said Martinez.

“Tonight it is easy to say the coach [is to blame], easy to say the players, but also we have to see other areas.”

Red Devils minority owner Jim Ratcliffe was at the stadium to watch the league-phase defeat by last season’s semi-finalists.

Man United spent around 140 million pounds ($185m) this summer on midfielders Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, but fans were upset the club did not reinforce other positions, including left-back and striker.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Carrick said he had not heard Martinez’s comments and so could not judge them.

“I think it’s a little bit on the emotions of the game as well, of coming here and being disappointed not to get something from the game,” said the coach.

Former Manchester United and England striker Wayne Rooney said Martinez’s criticism was excessive.

“I think he’s maybe gone a bit too far, and that should have stayed internal,” Rooney told Amazon Prime.

“You can clearly see that he cares and he wants the club to invest more money in more players, and to do that he’s probably one of the players who’ll be out the door if I’m being honest.”

articles.title: España deja escapar viva a Estados Unidos
articles.standfirst: Los goles de Alexia y Salma fueron replicados con los de Sánchez y Swanson para dejar el choque en tablas
articles.summary: Los goles de Alexia y Salma fueron replicados con los de Sánchez y Swanson para dejar el choque en tablas
articles.body: Estados Unidos y España firmaron tablas (2-2) en el segundo duelo entre ambas potencias en esta ventana internacional, esta vez con el Subaru Park de Chester como escenario de juego. Los goles de Alexia y Salma en la primera parte fueron respondidos con los tantos de Sánchez y Swanson, éste a sólo cinco minutos para el final. Sonia hizo seis cambios respecto al once que alineó en Washington tres días antes, tocando todas las líneas, pero la puesta en escena no varió mucho respecto al primer envite. Ambas selecciones apostaron por un duelo con gran intensidad y velocidad intentando desdibujar la pizarra rival, con una Estados Unidos combinando las transiciones con jugadas más elaboradas y una España solidaria en defensa y efectiva en el plano ofensivo. La primera ocasión del encuentro llevó la firma de Pinedo, que aprovechó un pase filtrado de Alexia para probar a Tullis-Joyce con un disparo cruzado que la jugadora del Manchester United salvó con un manotazo cual portera de balonmano. España tomó ventaja con dos goles en cinco minutos. Primero fue Alexia quien celebró su partido 150 como internacional con un tanto gestado en una jugada en la que Serrajordi puso el centro desde la diestra, Pinedo dejó pasar el balón entre sus piernas en el primer palo y la de Mollet del Vallès sólo tuvo que empujarla. Luego sería Putellas la que ejercería de asistente para una Salma que, con la diestra y tras golpear en el travesaño, metía de nuevo el balón en la jaula yanqui. Estados Unidos redujo distancias nada más reanudarse el choque en una jugada con polémica, dado que nació en una contra en la que Wilson golpeó la cara de Paredes y que finalizó con un disparo cruzado de Sánchez batiendo a Misa. Pasada la hora, ambas seleccionadoras agitaron el avispero con la entrada masiva de jugadoras. Swanson, una de esas permutas, tuvo el empate en sus botas en una contra, pero Misa salvó el momento de apuro. Las locales buscaron el empate con todo y consiguieron el premio del gol a sólo cinco minutos para el final. Un balón en largo fue controlado por Cooper dentro del área y esta asistió a Swanson para que cruzara el balón allá donde la meta española no pudiera alcanzar. En los siete minutos de añadido, los dos equipos fueron a por el partido sin premio. La más clara fue un disparo sobre la bocina de Yohannes que golpeó en Guijarro y Misa logró sacar en un gran acto de reflejos. España cerró el partido con sabor agridulce sabedora de que había dejado escapar viva a su rival, pero con buenas sensaciones la ventana internacional de la que aprender camino del Mundial del próximo verano.

articles.title: Alexia Putellas: el reinado continúa
articles.standfirst: La de Mollet del Vallès es la primera española que alcanza las 150 internacionalidades
articles.summary: La de Mollet del Vallès es la primera española que alcanza las 150 internacionalidades
articles.body: Alexia Putellas cumplió su partido 150 con la selección española en el empate ante Estados Unidos en Chester. La dos veces Balón de Oro firma un recorrido de 4.856 días con la selección absoluta desde que debutara el 28 de junio de 2013 en un amistoso ante Dinamarca en Velje en los que ha conquistado un Mundial, dos Nations League -torneos oficiales-, una Copa Algarve y una Copa Chipre -torneos oficiosos-. Alexia debutó hace más de 13 años con la selección partiendo desde el banquillo y con el dorsal '12' a la espalda, el primero de los seis dorsales que ha lucido con la elástica nacional -junto al '3', '20, '21', '14' y el '11' que lleva como marca registrada-. En total ha jugado 150 partidos en los que ha firmado 104 victorias, 24 empates y 22 derrotas. "Me siento con mucha energía, inquietudes, ganas de seguir aprendiendo, de continuar retándome. Ojalá seguir sana para seguir amando y haciendo lo que más me gusta y me hace feliz que es jugar al fútbol", dijo recientemente la protagonista en una entrevista para el Universo MARCA. Alexia alcanzó las 50 internacionalidades, por las que la RFEF hace a las jugadoras de un obsequio y una camiseta conmemorativa, el 28 de noviembre de 2017, en Mallorca y ante Austria, en un partido clasificatorio para el Mundial de Francia. La de Mollet del Vallès se convertiría en centenaria -la primera en lograrlo- el 1 de julio de 2022, en Castel di Sangro ante Italia, en un amistoso previo a la Eurocopa que finalmente no pudo disputar al romperse el LCA de la rodilla izquierda. Sin duda, su momento más triste con la selección. Alexia es la española con más internacionalidades (150) seguida de Irene Paredes (128), Jenni Hermoso (125), Mariona Caldentey (104), Aitana Bonmatí (89) y Marta Torrejón (89). Y aunque su marca pueda resultar amplia, aún está alejada de las jugadoras con más internacionalidades de los países ubicados en el top ten del ranking FIFA: la estadounidense Kristine Lilly (354) [récord absoluto], la canadiense Christine Sinclair (331), la sueca Caroline Seger (240), la brasileña Formiga (217), la alemana Birgit Prinz (214), la danesa Katrine Pedersen (210), la japonesa Homare Sawa (205), la francesa Eugénie Le Sommer (200), la inglesa Fara Williams (172). Alexia ha anotado, además, 43 goles con la selección española, siendo la segunda máxima goleadora histórica -sólo por detrás de Jenni Hermoso (57)-, superando a otras leyendas de nuestro país como Vero Boquete (38), Esther González (37), Adriana Martín (33) o Mar Prieto (32). La todocampista anotó su primer gol en su segundo partido internacional, en la Eurocopa de 2013 ante Inglaterra en Linköping; el último lo marcó ante Estados Unidos, a quien sumó a su listado de víctimas. "Todos sabemos quién es Alexia, una referente tanto dentro como fuera. Es una inspiración para las nuevas generaciones", dijo la seleccionadora Sonia Bermúdez. "Nos queda mucha Alexia para rato", añadió. Y es que el reinado continúa y los números de la leyenda incrementarán.

articles.title: Lisandro Martinez blasts Manchester United hierarchy in fiery rant; Wayne Rooney brands comments ‘disrespectful’ after UCL loss to Atletico Madrid
articles.summary: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has sparked controversy after openly criticising the club’s hierarchy following a 2-0 Champions League defeat
articles.body: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has sparked controversy after openly criticising the club’s hierarchy following a 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid, with former United captain Wayne Rooney accusing the Argentine of being disrespectful to his teammates.The defender’s post-match interview raised questions about United’s summer recruitment strategy and the club’s readiness to compete at the highest level. Martinez expressed frustration with the lack of further investment in the squad, suggesting that the club’s decision-makers should have done more after the team secured its return to the Champions League.Speaking to Amazon Prime, Martinez said: “I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it’s a reflection in the mirror of how is our club at the moment,” Martinez told Amazon Prime. “We did a fantastic season last season. And now we expect more from the top, from up, to bring more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well, and today also Atletico they have an amazing team and they deserved to win today.“I expect more from our technical director. I would have to be honest, as the players, we have to do more, but it’s just important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.”United, under director of football Jason Wilcox, reportedly invested around $213 million during the summer transfer window, bringing in players including Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite that spending, the club has endured a disappointing start to the campaign.The defeat in Madrid extended United’s winless streak across all competitions to five matches. The team has managed just one Premier League victory and currently sits 13th in the standings.Martinez also reflected on the contrast between last season’s progress and the team’s current struggles, expressing disappointment with the performance in Spain.“Last season we did everything; we created the base to be an amazing team,” Martinez said. “It's annoying, disappointing to come here and I'm not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here, it's disappointing.”Atletico made an immediate impact, with Pablo Barrios scoring in the opening minute before Ademola Lookman added a second-half goal to secure the victory. The result has increased scrutiny on United head coach Michael Carrick as the club attempts to recover from its difficult start.However, Martinez suggested that the focus on managerial changes overlooks other issues within the organisation.“You start changing, changing, changing manager. But what about other areas?” Martinez said. “I can’t say more.”Wayne Rooney questions Martinez’s motivesRooney strongly disagreed with Martinez’s decision to air his frustrations publicly, arguing that concerns about recruitment and squad quality should be discussed internally rather than through the media.Speaking on Amazon Prime after the match, the former United striker said: "I actually disagree as I thought it was a good performance."It's a difficult one because I always used to feel like I was outspoken as a player, and you want to have your opinion, but I think he's maybe gone too far; that should be down to the manager, and that should stay internal because the fans want to hear the players speak and they want to see them care."He clearly cares and wants the club to invest more money and more players, and if they do that, I think he'll be one of the players out the door if I'm being honest with his performances."His performances haven't been good enough but I think in some ways he is right, in terms of the club need to invest more at the top end of the pitch and in defence as well."I think it looks like that was a bit of an agenda from him because that doesn't mirror the performance. I thought the performance was better."Although Rooney acknowledged that United need improvements in key areas, he questioned why Martinez chose that particular moment to make his concerns public."I think Martinez was very premeditated. Why is he doing the interview after this game? Has he put himself forward, I very rarely hear him speak."It looked a bit premeditated and something he spoke about with his team to get out there. It's sad because when you need everyone to stick together as players, you can't be told what's going on above you."So you need them players, the manager, the coaching staff to stick together when you're having a difficult time; otherwise, something like that will rip a dressing room apart."I think it's a bit disrespectful to his team-mates as well because he's disrespecting his team-mates, he's saying they're not good enough. So he's saying his team-mates aren't good enough, so it's disrespectful."Rooney also suggested that captain Bruno Fernandes would be better placed to raise concerns on behalf of the squad, while insisting that any issues should be addressed privately."I think Bruno is probably the only one who has any right coming out and saying something like that if I'm being honest as captain. And even then, it should be behind closed doors if there are issues, which does happen."Players have conversations with the manager, the manager then has a conversation with the board, but that interview there, it's not going to help the situation the club is in at the minute."Now all that's going to bring is more noise around it, the players are unhappy, they're unsettled, they don't trust in their own team-mates, that's not going to help at all."Rooney draws on his own experienceRooney went further when discussing whether Martinez was attempting to reflect the frustrations of Manchester United supporters. While expressing appreciation for the defender’s ability, he pointed to his injury record and questioned whether he had done enough to speak on behalf of the squad."I don't think he's really connected with the fans since he's been here, to be honest, because he's been injured a lot."I actually like him, I think he's a good player, but he's been injured, so for the money the Man United pay for him, he hasn't given the service back really."From that point of view, that's not me being disrespectful, I just think he's had a lot of injuries and hasn't played that much."So I think he's trying to speak on behalf of the players if you like, but I think he's done it in the wrong way, as I said before, I think that should be from the captain if that's the case."For me, it's disrespectful to his teammates. I had a similar situation when I went in and asked Alex Ferguson about what players we were bringing in, and I apologised two days later."So I can speak from experience of what he's just done, I think it is very disrespectful, there's a lot of young players in that dressing room as well that need some guidance from experienced players."Drawing on his own playing career, Rooney argued that experienced footballers have a responsibility to guide younger teammates, particularly during difficult periods. He also indicated that the club’s board may need to respond to Martinez’s remarks."The board have to look at that, and they probably have to take some action on that, because that's just disrespecting the whole football club."Yes, there's issues, everyone wants more players and better players, but this is the players you've got. As a player, you've got to get on with it."You've got to go and show why you're a World Cup winner, as I said before.
